metadata.name: [GCP Cloud SQL PostgreSQL OTel] Read replica lag high
metadata.description: Alerts when a PostgreSQL read replica stays at least 120 seconds behind its primary for the whole 15-minute window (minimum lag at or above the threshold), for 2 consecutive checks. Optional metric: replica_lag is only reported on replica instances, so the rule is silent for instances without replicas. Requires at least 5 lag samples and applies the PostgreSQL engine marker (num_backends reported, or no MySQL/SQL Server-only network/connections in the window, so replicas missing some engine metrics stay covered). Grouped by the replica's database_id.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.cloudsql_postgresql.otel-*
| WHERE gcp.resource_type == "cloudsql_database"
// replica_lag (seconds) is reported on the REPLICA instance only; the rule is
// silent for instances without read replicas.
// MIN(MIN_OVER_TIME) and MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME) are exact across fragments.
| STATS lag_min = MIN(MIN_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/replication/replica_lag`)),
        lag_max = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/replication/replica_lag`)),
        network_lag_max = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/replication/network_lag`)),
        lag_n = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/replication/replica_lag`)),
        pg = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/postgresql/num_backends`)),
        conn = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/network/connections`))
    BY database_id

data.content:
## Cloud SQL PostgreSQL read replica lag high

The replica is persistently behind its primary: reads from it are stale, and if lag keeps growing the primary retains WAL, which can fill its disk.

### Triage
1. Compare `lag_max` with `network_lag_max`: if network lag dominates, check cross-region networking; otherwise the replica cannot replay fast enough.
2. Check the replica's CPU and disk I/O (replay is single-threaded) and look for long queries on the replica that conflict with replay.
3. Check the primary for a write burst (bulk load, large index build, VACUUM FULL) and its disk utilization.
4. Consider a larger replica tier, or redirect latency-sensitive reads to the primary until it catches up.

### Tuning
- Lower the threshold for latency-sensitive read traffic; raise it for cross-region replicas or batch-heavy primaries.
